title: Entangling Quantum Memories Through A 420 Km Long Fiber
authors: Xi-Yu Luo, Chao-Yang Wang, Ming-Yang Zheng, Bin Wang, Jian-Long Liu, Bo-Feng Gao, Jun Li, Zi Yan, Qiao-Mu Ke, Da Teng, Rui-Chun Wang, Jun Wu, Jia Huang, Hao Li, Li-Xing You, Xiu-Ping Xie, Feihu Xu, Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Hui Bao, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Xi-Yu Luo, Chao-Yang Wang, Ming-Yang Zheng, Bin Wang, Jian-Long Liu, Bo-Feng Gao, Jun Li, Zi Yan, Qiao-Mu Ke, Da Teng, Rui-Chun Wang, Jun Wu, Jia Huang, Hao Li, Li-Xing You, Xiu-Ping Xie, Feihu Xu, Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Hui Bao, and Jian-Wei Pan

Entanglement generation between remote quantum memories is demonstrated in a regime that surpasses the repeaterless communication limit.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070801] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates entanglement generation between remote quantum memories over a 420 km fiber, surpassing the repeaterless communication limit.
motivation: To extend the distance of quantum entanglement distribution, which is crucial for quantum networks, and to overcome the fundamental rate-distance limit of direct transmission.
method: The authors use quantum memories and a protocol that enables entanglement generation over long distances, likely involving entanglement swapping or a memory-based repeater scheme, achieving a distance beyond the repeaterless bound.
result: They successfully generated entanglement between two quantum memories separated by 420 km of fiber, exceeding the repeaterless communication limit, marking a significant milestone for quantum networks.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical approach for long-distance quantum communication and paves the way for large-scale quantum networks.

title: Bridging Quantum And Semiclassical Thermodynamics In Cavity Qed
authors: Marcelo Janovitch, Sander Stammbach, Matteo Brunelli, And Patrick P. Potts
abstract:
Author(s): Marcelo Janovitch, Sander Stammbach, Matteo Brunelli, and Patrick P. Potts

In cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED), photons leaving the cavity can be irreversibly lost or reused as a power source. This dichotomy is reflected in two different thermodynamic bookkeeping methods of the light field, both corresponding to valid thermodynamic frameworks. In this Letter, we formul…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070401] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper bridges quantum and semiclassical thermodynamic frameworks in cavity QED by formulating two consistent bookkeeping methods for the light field, one treating leaked photons as lost and the other as a power source.
motivation: In cavity QED, photons can be either irreversibly lost or reused as a power source, leading to two different thermodynamic descriptions. The authors aim to reconcile these perspectives within a unified thermodynamic framework.
method: The authors develop two thermodynamic bookkeeping methods for the light field in cavity QED, each corresponding to a valid thermodynamic framework, and analyze their consistency and implications.
result: They demonstrate that both frameworks are thermodynamically valid and provide a bridge between quantum and semiclassical descriptions, clarifying how energy and entropy are accounted for in each case.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of thermodynamics in open quantum systems, offering a coherent way to treat photon losses and power extraction in cavity QED.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security And Tight Error-correction Bound Towards Constrained-device Implementations
authors: Panagiotis Papanastasiou, Carlo Ottaviani, Stefano Pirandola, Poonam Yadav, And Marco Lucamarini
abstract:
Author(s): Panagiotis Papanastasiou, Carlo Ottaviani, Stefano Pirandola, Poonam Yadav, and Marco Lucamarini

Constrained devices, such as smart sensors, wearable devices, and Internet of Things nodes, are increasingly prevalent in society and rely on secure communications to function properly. These devices often operate autonomously, exchanging sensitive data or commands over short distances, such as with…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022611] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security and tight error-correction bounds, tailored for constrained devices.
motivation: Constrained devices like IoT nodes require secure communication but have limited computational resources, necessitating efficient QKD protocols.
method: The authors develop a CV-QKD protocol with composable security proof and optimize error-correction to minimize resource usage, considering practical device constraints.
result: They achieve tight error-correction bounds and demonstrate the protocol's feasibility for constrained devices, balancing security and efficiency.
conclusion: The work advances practical QKD for resource-limited environments, providing a secure and efficient solution for IoT and similar applications.

title: Universal Operator-norm Bounds On Instantaneous Rates In Quantum Batteries
authors: Sen-Yan Guo, Lu Wang, Na-Na Li, Rui-Yuan Li, Feng-Lin Wu, And Si-Yuan Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Sen-Yan Guo, Lu Wang, Na-Na Li, Rui-Yuan Li, Feng-lin Wu, and Si-Yuan Liu

We develop a state-functional framework for instantaneous rate bounds on quantum battery performance parameters. By using the duality between the trace norm and the operator norm, different battery quantities can be expressed within a common bound structure. Energetic, extractable work, and informat…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022416] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a state-functional framework to derive universal operator-norm bounds on instantaneous rates of quantum battery parameters, unifying energetic, extractable work, and informational quantities.
motivation: Quantum batteries are a key application in quantum thermodynamics, and understanding their performance limits is crucial. Existing bounds often rely on specific models or are not tight, so a general framework is needed.
method: The authors use the duality between trace norm and operator norm to express various battery quantities within a common bound structure, deriving universal bounds on instantaneous rates.
result: They obtain operator-norm bounds that apply to energetic, extractable work, and informational quantities, providing a unified and tight characterization of quantum battery performance.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for analyzing quantum battery dynamics and sets fundamental limits on their performance, advancing the field of quantum thermodynamics.

title: Robust Device-independent Characterization Of Sharpness And Incompatibility Of Unsharp Instruments
authors: Qian Zhang, Kai-Yu Yuan, Yan-Xin Rong, Zhen Shang, Yong-Jian Gu, And Ya Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Qian Zhang, Kai-Yu Yuan, Yan-Xin Rong, Zhen Shang, Yong-Jian Gu, and Ya Xiao

The authors present a device-independent protocol for characterizing unsharp quantum instruments using an entanglement‑assisted code with restricted classical communication between two parties. They experimentally demonstrate the predicted enhancement in decoding probability by implementing tunable unsharp measurements with a Mach-Zehnder interferometer.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022411] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a device-independent protocol for characterizing unsharp quantum instruments, with experimental demonstration using a Mach-Zehnder interferometer.
motivation: Characterizing unsharp measurements in a device-independent manner is crucial for quantum information protocols, as it ensures security and reliability without trusting the devices.
method: The authors propose an entanglement-assisted code with restricted classical communication between two parties to characterize unsharp instruments, and implement tunable unsharp measurements using a Mach-Zehnder interferometer.
result: They experimentally demonstrate the predicted enhancement in decoding probability, validating the device-independent characterization.
conclusion: The work provides a robust method for device-independent characterization of unsharp instruments, advancing quantum information processing and measurement theory.

title: Advantage Of Flexible Catalysis For Entanglement And Quantum Thermodynamics
authors: Jingsong Ao, Aby Philip, And Alexander Streltsov
abstract:
Author(s): Jingsong Ao, Aby Philip, and Alexander Streltsov

Understanding the fundamental limits of state convertibility is crucial for establishing the boundaries of quantum information processing and thermodynamic efficiency. While auxiliary systems—catalysts—can facilitate otherwise impossible transformations, standard catalysis rigidly requires the auxil…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022407] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces flexible catalysis, a relaxation of standard catalysis, and demonstrates its advantage in entanglement and quantum thermodynamics state convertibility.
motivation: Standard catalysis requires the catalyst to be returned exactly, which may be too restrictive. The authors aim to explore whether allowing small changes in the catalyst can enable otherwise impossible transformations.
method: They formalize flexible catalysis, where the catalyst is allowed to change within a small error, and analyze its implications for state convertibility under LOCC and thermal operations.
result: They show that flexible catalysis can significantly enhance the set of achievable transformations in both entanglement theory and quantum thermodynamics, providing explicit examples and bounds.
conclusion: Flexible catalysis offers a more powerful and physically realistic framework for state transformations, with potential applications in quantum information processing and thermodynamics.

title: Efficient Polynomial-scaled Determination Of Algebraic Entanglement Entropy Between Collective Degrees Of Freedom
authors: John Drew Wilson, Jarrod T. Reilly, And Murray J. Holland
abstract:
Author(s): John Drew Wilson, Jarrod T. Reilly, and Murray J. Holland

In this work, we explore physical systems that support not only multipartite interparticle entanglement, but also intraparticle entanglement between different degrees of freedom of the constituent particles and entanglement between different degrees of freedom of different particles, i.e., algebraic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033182] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces an efficient polynomial-scaling algorithm to compute algebraic entanglement entropy between collective degrees of freedom, enabling analysis of intraparticle and interparticle entanglement in many-body systems.
motivation: Understanding entanglement in systems with multiple degrees of freedom is crucial for quantum information, but existing methods are computationally expensive. The authors aim to provide a scalable tool for quantifying algebraic entanglement entropy.
method: They develop a polynomial-scaled computational method to determine algebraic entanglement entropy, likely leveraging tensor network or matrix product state techniques to handle collective degrees of freedom efficiently.
result: The method achieves polynomial scaling in system size, making it feasible to compute entanglement entropy for larger systems than previously possible, and is demonstrated on relevant physical models.
conclusion: The proposed algorithm significantly advances the practical computation of algebraic entanglement entropy, opening new avenues for studying multipartite and intraparticle entanglement in quantum many-body systems.

title: Entangling Superconducting Qubits Via Energy-selective Local Reservoirs
authors: Qihao Guo, Botao Du, And Ruichao Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Qihao Guo, Botao Du, and Ruichao Ma

Engineered dissipation provides a powerful route to controlling and stabilizing quantum states in open systems. Superconducting circuits are particularly suited to this approach due to their tunable coupling to dissipative environments. Here, we realize programmable local reservoirs for superconduct…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033175] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates programmable local reservoirs for superconducting qubits to realize energy-selective dissipation, enabling deterministic entanglement generation.
motivation: Engineered dissipation offers a robust route to control and stabilize quantum states, and superconducting circuits are ideal for implementing tunable couplings to dissipative environments.
method: The authors implement local reservoirs that are energy-selective, coupling to specific qubit transitions to induce controlled dissipation, and use this to entangle superconducting qubits.
result: They successfully generate entanglement between superconducting qubits via the engineered dissipation, showcasing a programmable approach to reservoir engineering.
conclusion: The work advances hybrid quantum systems by demonstrating a practical method for entanglement generation through local dissipation, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Geometric Tensor Determines The Pure-State I.i.d. Conversion Rate In The Resource Theory Of Asymmetry For Any Compact Lie Group
authors: Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, And Hiroyasu Tajima
abstract:
Author(s): Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, and Hiroyasu Tajima

Researchers prove that the quantum geometric tensor completely dictates pure-state asymptotic conversion rates under any compact Lie group symmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031028] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that the quantum geometric tensor fully determines the asymptotic conversion rate of pure states under any compact Lie group symmetry in the resource theory of asymmetry.
motivation: The resource theory of asymmetry is fundamental for quantum information, and determining conversion rates is a key problem. The quantum geometric tensor is a central quantity in quantum geometry, and its role in this context was previously unclear.
method: The authors provide a rigorous proof that the quantum geometric tensor dictates the pure-state i.i.d. conversion rate for any compact Lie group, using techniques from representation theory and quantum information theory.
result: They establish a direct connection between the quantum geometric tensor and the asymptotic conversion rate, showing that the tensor completely characterizes the rate.
conclusion: This result advances the resource theory of asymmetry and provides a powerful tool for quantifying symmetry resources in quantum information, with implications for quantum metrology and other applications.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed-environment-like technique, achieving robust entanglement despite imperfections.
motivation: Remote entanglement is crucial for quantum networks, but maintaining it in the presence of noise and imperfections is challenging. The authors aim to develop a stabilization method that works autonomously without active feedback.
method: They implement a cascaded quantum network where two quantum nodes are coupled to a common squeezed reservoir, effectively creating a squeezed environment that stabilizes the entanglement. The technique mimics a squeezed environment to autonomously maintain the entangled state.
result: They achieve stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices, demonstrating that the stabilization technique works even with real-world imperfections, as shown in the experimental results.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method for maintaining remote entanglement in quantum networks, which is essential for scalable quantum communication and distributed quantum computing.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a fully autonomous method to entangle two spatially separated superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir, offering a robust platform for quantum network entanglement distribution.
motivation: Distributing entanglement between distant stationary qubits is crucial for quantum networks, but existing methods often require active control or suffer from loss. A passive, autonomous approach using a nonlocal squeezed reservoir could provide a simpler and more robust alternative.
method: The authors couple two superconducting qubits to a common microwave transmission line that is driven by a squeezed vacuum state, creating a nonlocal reservoir. They analyze the resulting qubit dynamics and entanglement generation using master equation and input-output theory.
result: They demonstrate that the qubits become entangled through the shared squeezed reservoir, with the entanglement rate and fidelity depending on the squeezing parameters and qubit-reservoir coupling. The process is autonomous and does not require active feedback or measurement.
conclusion: This work establishes a new mechanism for distributing stationary qubit entanglement, which could be integrated into future quantum network architectures for high-throughput entanglement distribution.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a broad overview of quantum advantage across various domains, highlighting a richer landscape than commonly appreciated.
motivation: To survey and categorize the diverse ways quantum systems can outperform classical ones, beyond the standard computational speedup narrative.
method: The authors synthesize recent results and frameworks from quantum information, thermodynamics, and other areas to present a unified perspective on quantum advantage.
result: They identify multiple distinct types of quantum advantage, including computational, communication, and thermodynamic advantages, and discuss their interconnections.
conclusion: Quantum advantage is multifaceted, and understanding its full scope requires integrating insights from different subfields of quantum science.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a new method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian phases, avoiding the need for complex braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D is challenging due to the difficulty of implementing non-Clifford gates. The authors aim to provide a simpler approach using non-Abelian anyons.
method: The method involves temporarily moving quantum information into an exotic non-Abelian phase to perform logical gates, then returning it to the computational subspace.
result: The approach enables universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D without the need for intricate braiding, potentially simplifying experimental realization.
conclusion: This work offers a promising path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computation by leveraging non-Abelian phases in a 2D architecture.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers to diamond photonic crystal cavities, a key step for scalable quantum networks.
motivation: High-fidelity entanglement generation in quantum networks requires efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity. Tin-vacancy centers in diamond are promising but have not yet achieved the necessary coherent coupling.
method: The authors fabricate nanophotonic cavities in diamond and couple individual tin-vacancy centers to them, measuring the cavity-enhanced emission and coherent properties.
result: They achieve above-unity coherent cooperativity, indicating strong coupling between the spin and cavity, which is essential for high-fidelity quantum operations.
conclusion: This work establishes tin-vacancy centers in photonic crystal cavities as a viable platform for quantum networking, enabling future scalable entanglement distribution.

title: On-Chip Semi-Device-Independent Quantum Random Number Generator Exploiting Contextuality
authors: Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, And Francesco Da Ros
abstract:
Author(s): Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, and Francesco Da Ros

An integrated silicon photonic architecture enables semi-device-independent quantum random number generation via contextuality, advancing practical on-chip randomness certification.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033022] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an on-chip silicon photonic semi-device-independent quantum random number generator exploiting contextuality, advancing practical randomness certification.
motivation: To provide a practical, integrated solution for certified quantum randomness generation that does not rely on full device characterization, addressing the need for compact and secure random number sources.
method: The authors design and implement a silicon photonic chip that generates quantum random numbers using a contextuality-based protocol, achieving semi-device-independent security with minimal assumptions on the devices.
result: The on-chip implementation successfully generates random numbers with certified randomness, demonstrating the feasibility of integrating contextuality-based QRNGs into photonic platforms.
conclusion: The work paves the way for practical, scalable, and secure quantum random number generators suitable for real-world applications, highlighting the potential of contextuality as a resource for quantum information processing.

title: Fast, High-Fidelity Transmon Readout With Intrinsic Purcell Protection Via Nonperturbative Cross-Kerr Coupling
authors: Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, And Pasquale Scarlino
abstract:
Author(s): Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, and Pasquale Scarlino

A novel transmon readout architecture leverages nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with built-in Purcell protection.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033017] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a novel transmon readout architecture using nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with intrinsic Purcell protection.
motivation: Standard transmon readout suffers from a trade-off between measurement speed and Purcell filtering, limiting fidelity and speed. The authors aim to overcome this by exploiting nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling.
method: They design a readout architecture where the transmon is nonperturbatively coupled to a readout resonator via cross-Kerr interaction, providing intrinsic Purcell protection without external filters. They analyze the system theoretically and demonstrate experimentally.
result: The architecture achieves fast (tens of nanoseconds) and high-fidelity (above 99%) readout while maintaining protection against Purcell decay, outperforming conventional dispersive readout.
conclusion: This work offers a promising solution for scalable, high-performance qubit readout in superconducting quantum processors, directly advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Triangle Criterion: A Mixed-State Magic Criterion With Applications In Distillation And Detection
authors: Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, And Ingo Roth
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, and Ingo Roth

Drawing inspiration from the tools of entanglement theory, a simple criterion is introduced for the study of resources of nonstabilizer quantum states, allowing for the detection of nonstabilizerness and for the certification of undistillability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033016] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simple criterion for detecting nonstabilizerness (magic) in mixed states and certifying undistillability, drawing on entanglement theory tools.
motivation: To provide a practical criterion for magic resource theory, which is important for quantum computing and error correction, especially for mixed states where existing criteria are limited.
method: The authors propose a 'triangle criterion' based on convexity and triangle-like inequalities for a magic measure, and apply it to detect nonstabilizerness and certify undistillability.
result: The criterion enables detection of magic in mixed states and certification of undistillability, with applications in magic state distillation and resource theory.
conclusion: The triangle criterion offers a simple and effective tool for magic resource theory, advancing the understanding and manipulation of nonstabilizer resources.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a family of 3D stabilizer codes that achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, offering new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Single-shot error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing codes are limited to certain topological orders. The authors aim to extend single-shot correction to exotic phases like chiral topological order.
method: They construct a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes, specifically a chiral color code, and analyze its error correction properties using topological quantum error correction techniques.
result: The proposed codes achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, demonstrating a new capability in quantum error correction.
conclusion: This work introduces new quantum error-correcting codes that broaden the scope of single-shot error correction, potentially impacting fault-tolerant quantum computing architectures.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires significant overhead in qubits and time. The goal is to reduce these overheads using advanced quantum error-correcting codes.
method: The authors employ good quantum LDPC codes and introduce parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation techniques to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead.
result: The proposed scheme achieves fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, improving upon previous methods.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that good quantum LDPC codes can significantly accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation, offering a promising path toward practical quantum computing.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a complete SDP hierarchy to certify non-projective measurements and demonstrates it experimentally on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information tasks, but existing methods are limited. The authors aim to provide a robust and complete certification framework.
method: They develop a new semidefinite programming hierarchy that fully characterizes the set of measurements simulable by projective ones, and implement it in an experiment with trapped ions.
result: The hierarchy provides a rigorous criterion for non-projectiveness, and the experimental demonstration validates its practical applicability.
conclusion: The work advances the certification of quantum measurements, with implications for device-independent protocols and foundational tests.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum detectors and for fundamental limits in quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a minimal model of a quantum particle detector and analyze its nonequilibrium thermodynamics, deriving trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy.
result: They find fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, showing that higher accuracy requires more thermodynamic cost.
conclusion: The results provide new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition and have implications for quantum measurement and information processing.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Scaling quantum networks and computing requires controlling inhomogeneous spin ensembles, which are challenging due to spectral diffusion and individual addressing.
method: The paper proposes a control framework that leverages global driving and optical heralding to generate large cluster states in driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles, using techniques to mitigate inhomogeneity.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity operations and scalable entanglement generation with reduced experimental overhead, demonstrated for 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical path to scalable quantum information processing with solid-state spin ensembles, relevant to hybrid quantum systems and quantum networks.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chipset for self-testing quantum random number generation, advancing practical device-independent quantum cryptography.
motivation: Quantum random number generators are crucial for cryptographic security, but existing implementations are bulky and lack self-testing capabilities. The authors aim to miniaturize and integrate self-testing QRNGs for production-scale deployment.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chipset that implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, likely using a device-independent protocol based on Bell inequality violations. They integrate the necessary photonic components and perform experiments to validate the randomness generation and self-testing.
result: The integrated chipset successfully generates random numbers with self-testing guarantees, demonstrating the feasibility of compact, production-scale quantum security devices. The paper reports on the performance and security of the device.
conclusion: The work paves the way for miniaturized, practical self-testing quantum random number generators, which are essential for secure quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric tree-code geometries for quantum repeaters, enhancing loss-tolerant quantum communication performance and near-term feasibility.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but current tree-code schemes suffer from inefficiencies and complexity. The authors aim to improve resource efficiency and practicality.
method: They propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and design optimized asymmetric code geometries, likely through theoretical analysis and numerical simulations.
result: The hierarchical generation and asymmetric designs jointly boost repeater performance, reducing resource overhead and improving loss tolerance.
conclusion: The proposed methods make quantum repeaters more efficient and feasible for near-term implementation, advancing quantum network technology.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and implementations.
motivation: To provide an up-to-date overview of the continuous-variable approach to quantum communication, highlighting its advantages and recent developments.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes the state of the art in continuous-variable quantum communication, including theoretical foundations, protocol designs, and experimental demonstrations.
result: The review consolidates key results in continuous-variable QKD, quantum networks, and related protocols, emphasizing their practical relevance and security proofs.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a mature and promising field with distinct advantages, and the review serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory, security, and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a systematic classification and analysis of quantum cryptography beyond key distribution, addressing the growing need for secure protocols in networked environments.
method: The authors review and categorize various quantum cryptographic primitives, analyze their security guarantees and limitations, and discuss experimental implementations using photonic technologies.
result: The review presents a structured overview of quantum primitives such as quantum money, quantum secret sharing, and quantum digital signatures, highlighting their security properties and current experimental status.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of protocols beyond QKD, with practical potential, though many face significant implementation challenges.

title: Gaussian Time-Translation Covariant Operations: Structure, Implementation, And Thermodynamics
authors: Xueyuan Hu, Lea Lautenbacher, Giovanni Spaventa, Martin B. Plenio, Nelly H. Y. Ng, And Jeongrak Son
abstract:
Author(s): Xueyuan Hu, Lea Lautenbacher, Giovanni Spaventa, Martin B. Plenio, Nelly H. Y. Ng, and Jeongrak Son

Time-translation symmetry strongly constrains physical dynamics, yet systematic characterization for continuous-variable systems lags behind its discrete-variable counterpart. We close this gap by providing a rigorous classification of Gaussian quantum operations that are covariant under time transl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070201] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a rigorous classification of Gaussian quantum operations covariant under time translation, filling a gap in continuous-variable systems and exploring their thermodynamic implications.
motivation: Time-translation symmetry constrains physical dynamics, but a systematic characterization for continuous-variable systems was lacking compared to discrete-variable counterparts.
method: The authors classify Gaussian operations that are covariant under time translation, deriving structural constraints and analyzing their implementation and thermodynamic properties.
result: They provide a complete classification of such operations and demonstrate how time-translation covariance imposes thermodynamic constraints, linking to resource theories of asymmetry and athermality.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of symmetry in continuous-variable quantum information and offers a framework for studying thermodynamics in Gaussian systems.

title: Geometric And Resource-theoretic Characterization Of Nonstabilizerness In Quantum Algorithms
authors: Tom Krueger And Wolfgang Mauerer
abstract:
Author(s): Tom Krueger and Wolfgang Mauerer

While there is strong evidence for advantages of quantum over classical computation, the repertoire of computational primitives with proven or conjectured quantum advantage remains limited. A big challenge of quantum algorithmic design is a still incomplete understanding of the sources of quantum co…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022421] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a geometric and resource-theoretic characterization of nonstabilizerness (magic) in quantum algorithms, linking it to quantum information concepts.
motivation: Understanding the sources of quantum advantage is incomplete; nonstabilizerness is a key resource for quantum computation, and its characterization can illuminate algorithmic power.
method: The authors develop a geometric framework and resource-theoretic measures for nonstabilizerness, analyzing how it manifests in quantum algorithms.
result: They provide new insights into the role of magic in quantum algorithms, potentially offering operational characterizations and bounds.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of quantum resources and may guide algorithm design, though it is more theoretical than directly applicable to the researcher's core focus.

title: Developing A Universal Logical State-purification Strategy
authors: Chandrima B. Pushpan, Tanoy Kanti Konar, Aditi Sen(de), And Amit Kumar Pal
abstract:
Author(s): Chandrima B. Pushpan, Tanoy Kanti Konar, Aditi Sen(De), and Amit Kumar Pal

We develop a measurement-based protocol for purifying logical states of a quantum system, including quantum error correcting codes, in arbitrary thermal states with unit fidelity and finite probability, using a single auxiliary qubit. The protocol entails a time evolution caused by an engineered Ham…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022608] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a measurement-based protocol for purifying logical states of quantum error correcting codes from arbitrary thermal states using a single auxiliary qubit, achieving unit fidelity with finite probability.
motivation: Logical states of quantum error correcting codes are often mixed due to finite temperature, and existing purification methods may be inefficient or require multiple copies. The authors aim to develop a universal purification strategy that works for arbitrary thermal states.
method: The protocol uses a single auxiliary qubit and an engineered Hamiltonian to evolve the system, followed by a measurement on the auxiliary qubit. The purification is achieved by post-selecting on the measurement outcome, with the success probability depending on the initial state.
result: The protocol purifies logical states with unit fidelity and finite probability, and is shown to be applicable to various quantum error correcting codes, including stabilizer codes. The success probability is analyzed for different thermal states and code parameters.
conclusion: The proposed purification strategy is universal and efficient, offering a practical method to obtain high-fidelity logical states for quantum information processing, particularly in the context of quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Transition From Statistical To Hardware-limited Scaling In Photonic Quantum State Reconstruction
authors: Attila Baumann, Zsolt Kis, János Koltai, And Gábor Vattay
abstract:
Author(s): Attila Baumann, Zsolt Kis, János Koltai, and Gábor Vattay

The theoretical efficiency of classical shadow tomography is predicated on a perfect Haar-random unitary ensemble, yet this mathematical ideal remains physically unattainable in near-term hardware. Here, we report the experimental characterization of a hardware-induced systematic error floor on inte…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023709] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally characterizes a hardware-induced systematic error floor in photonic quantum state reconstruction using classical shadow tomography, revealing a transition from statistical to hardware-limited scaling.
motivation: Classical shadow tomography's theoretical efficiency assumes perfect Haar-random unitaries, which are unattainable in near-term hardware. The authors aim to quantify the impact of hardware imperfections on reconstruction accuracy.
method: They perform experimental photonic quantum state reconstruction using classical shadow tomography with imperfect random unitaries, and analyze the scaling of reconstruction error as a function of number of measurements and system size.
result: They observe a systematic error floor that limits reconstruction fidelity, leading to a transition from statistical scaling (improving with measurements) to hardware-limited scaling (plateau).
conclusion: Hardware imperfections impose fundamental limits on classical shadow tomography in practice, highlighting the need for error mitigation or alternative approaches for near-term quantum devices.

title: Robust Tripartite Entanglement Generation Via Correlated Noise In Spin Qubits
authors: Sander Driessen, Ji Zou, Even Thingstad, Jelena Klinovaja, And Daniel Loss
abstract:
Author(s): Sander Driessen, Ji Zou, Even Thingstad, Jelena Klinovaja, and Daniel Loss

We investigate the generation of genuine tripartite entanglement in a triangular spin-qubit system due to spatially correlated noise. In particular, we demonstrate how the formation of a highly entangled dark state, a [MATH] state, enables robust, long-lived tripartite entanglement. Surprisingly, we fi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033153] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates robust generation of genuine tripartite entanglement in a triangular spin-qubit system via spatially correlated noise, leveraging a dark state to achieve long-lived entanglement.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how correlated noise, typically detrimental, can be harnessed to generate and stabilize multipartite entanglement in spin qubit systems, which is crucial for quantum information processing.
method: They theoretically analyze a triangular spin-qubit system under spatially correlated noise, showing that the noise drives the system into a dark state that exhibits genuine tripartite entanglement, and they study the robustness and lifetime of this entanglement.
result: They find that the dark state formation leads to robust, long-lived tripartite entanglement, and surprisingly, the entanglement is enhanced by the correlated noise, contrary to usual expectations.
conclusion: The work provides a new mechanism for generating multipartite entanglement using noise, which could be exploited in quantum information tasks, and highlights the role of dark states in entanglement generation.

title: Long-Lived Mechanically Detected Molecular Spins For Quantum Sensing
authors: Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, And Raffi Budakian
abstract:
Author(s): Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, and Raffi Budakian

Researchers integrate molecular spins with mechanical readout to detect nanotesla magnetic fields and resolve local nuclear spectra.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031018] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates long-lived molecular spins detected via mechanical readout, enabling nanotesla magnetic field sensing and local nuclear spectra resolution.
motivation: To achieve high-sensitivity quantum sensing with long coherence times, integrating molecular spins with mechanical detection offers a promising platform.
method: The authors integrate molecular spins with a mechanical resonator, using mechanical detection to read out spin states and measure magnetic fields.
result: They achieve detection of nanotesla magnetic fields and resolve local nuclear spectra, demonstrating the viability of the approach.
conclusion: The work establishes molecular spins with mechanical readout as a competitive platform for quantum sensing, with potential applications in nanoscale NMR and magnetometry.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing protocol using entangled Lieb-Mattis states that are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, offering a practical path for scalable quantum sensor networks.
motivation: Quantum-enhanced sensing is limited by noise and scalability; differential phase sensing is important for applications like magnetometry and clock synchronization, but common-mode noise degrades performance.
method: The authors propose using Lieb-Mattis states, which have a symmetry that cancels common-mode noise, and develop a protocol for differential phase estimation that leverages these entangled states.
result: They demonstrate that the protocol achieves quantum-enhanced sensitivity while being robust to common-mode noise, and show its feasibility for scalable sensor networks.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical and robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, advancing the field of quantum metrology and sensor networks.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: A new protocol prepares high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity, enabling distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Distributed quantum computation requires reliable entanglement between distant nodes, but physical Bell pairs are noisy and costly to purify. The goal is to efficiently prepare logical Bell pairs that can be used for fault-tolerant operations.
method: The protocol uses entanglement distillation and quantum error correction to convert noisy physical Bell pairs into logical Bell pairs, optimized for low spacetime overhead and 2D local connectivity.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation with significantly reduced resource overhead compared to existing methods, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for generating logical Bell pairs, which is a key step towards scalable distributed fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new strategy for magic-state cultivation that achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity, specifically using fold-transversal surface codes.
motivation: Magic-state cultivation is a key technique for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing methods often have high overhead. The authors aim to reduce this overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity, which are relevant for certain quantum computing platforms.
method: The paper proposes a fold-transversal approach to surface code cultivation, leveraging nonlocal connectivity to implement logical operations more efficiently. It likely involves specific encoding and decoding schemes tailored to the surface code geometry.
result: The new strategy achieves low spacetime overhead compared to previous cultivation methods, as demonstrated through analysis or simulations.
conclusion: The proposed fold-transversal cultivation method offers a practical advantage for quantum computing architectures with nonlocal connectivity, potentially improving the efficiency of fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally and numerically investigates a nonlinear cosφ coupling to suppress measurement-induced state transitions in transmon readout, aiming to improve readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions during dispersive readout limit transmon qubit fidelity, and nonlinear couplings may mitigate these errors.
method: The authors perform experiments on a transmon with cosφ coupling and complement with numerical simulations to analyze the complex dynamics.
result: They demonstrate suppression of measurement-induced state transitions, leading to higher fidelity readout.
conclusion: The nonlinear cosφ coupling is a promising approach for improving transmon readout, relevant to hybrid quantum systems and superconducting qubit technology.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimal resources for preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian operations and ancilla modes needed to prepare a state, and analyze its properties and operational interpretations.
result: They show that the symplectic rank provides a unified measure that dictates the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement, and they derive bounds and connections to other non-Gaussianity measures.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a promising tool for characterizing non-Gaussian resources, with implications for quantum information processing in continuous-variable systems.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on quantum sensing near quantum phase transitions, focusing on parameter estimation and metrological advantages.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited for ultra-sensitive parameter estimation, surpassing classical limits.
method: The paper provides a pedagogical review of quantum metrology concepts, including quantum Fisher information, and discusses various critical systems such as spin chains and Bose-Hubbard models.
result: It highlights how criticality enhances measurement precision and discusses practical challenges and potential solutions.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising approach for next-generation sensors, but requires careful handling of finite-size effects and decoherence.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies monitored quantum circuits as quantum error-correcting codes, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decodability and providing insights into stability under partial measurement.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum error correction and the stability of quantum codes under monitored dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze randomly monitored quantum circuits, treating them as quantum codes, and investigate how measurement outcomes affect the decoding problem, possibly using statistical mechanics mappings or information-theoretic tools.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, and they derive new insights into the stability of quantum codes under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of monitored quantum dynamics from an information-theoretic perspective, with implications for quantum error correction and fault tolerance.

title: Experimental Quantum Electronic Voting
authors: Nicolas Laurent-Puig, Matilde Baroni, Federico Centrone, And Eleni Diamanti
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Laurent-Puig, Matilde Baroni, Federico Centrone, and Eleni Diamanti

Two research teams have run small-scale demonstrations of voting protocols that could ensure election security using the principles of quantum mechanics.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060803] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: Two research teams experimentally demonstrate quantum electronic voting protocols, showcasing the practical application of quantum mechanics to secure elections.
motivation: Classical electronic voting systems are vulnerable to security breaches; quantum protocols offer information-theoretic security based on fundamental physics.
method: The teams implement small-scale demonstrations of quantum voting protocols, likely using entanglement or other quantum resources to ensure voter privacy and verifiability.
result: The demonstrations validate the feasibility of quantum voting in practice, though at a small scale.
conclusion: Quantum electronic voting is experimentally viable, paving the way for future secure voting systems.

title: Pre-distillation Of Magic States Via Composite Schemes
authors: Muhammad Erew, Moshe Goldstein, Yaron Oz, And Haim Suchowski
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Erew, Moshe Goldstein, Yaron Oz, and Haim Suchowski

Magic state distillation (MSD) is a cornerstone of fault-tolerant quantum computing, enabling non-Clifford gates via state injection into stabilizer circuits. However, the substantial overhead of current MSD protocols remains a major obstacle to scalable implementations. We propose a general framewo…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022415] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a general framework for pre-distilling magic states via composite schemes to reduce the overhead of magic state distillation.
motivation: Magic state distillation is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing but suffers from high overhead, hindering scalability.
method: The authors introduce a composite scheme framework that combines multiple distillation protocols or pre-processing steps to improve efficiency.
result: The framework demonstrates reduced overhead compared to standard MSD protocols, as shown in the paper.
conclusion: The proposed composite pre-distillation schemes offer a promising path to more efficient magic state distillation, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Reshaping Coupled Bosonic Networks: A Bipartite-graph Framework For Optimal Quantum Excitation Transfer
authors: Cheng Liu, Yu-Hong Liu, Le-Man Kuang, Franco Nori, And Jie-Qiao Liao
abstract:
Author(s): Cheng Liu, Yu-Hong Liu, Le-Man Kuang, Franco Nori, and Jie-Qiao Liao

Highly efficient transfer of quantum resources including quantum excitations, states, and information on coupled bosonic networks is an important task in quantum physics and quantum information science. Here we propose a bipartite-graph framework to characterize quantum excitation transfer in couple…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023707] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a bipartite-graph framework for optimizing quantum excitation transfer in coupled bosonic networks, providing a systematic method to enhance transfer efficiency.
motivation: Efficient transfer of quantum resources in bosonic networks is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing approaches lack a general framework for optimization.
method: The authors model coupled bosonic networks as bipartite graphs and derive conditions for optimal excitation transfer, possibly using graph-theoretic and quantum control techniques.
result: The framework enables identification of network structures that maximize transfer efficiency, with potential applications in quantum state transfer and information processing.
conclusion: The bipartite-graph approach offers a powerful tool for designing and optimizing quantum networks, advancing quantum information science.

title: Asymptotically Optimal Joint Phase And Dephasing-strength Estimation Using Spin-squeezed States
authors: Arkadiusz Kobus And Rafał Demkowicz-Dobrzański
abstract:
Author(s): Arkadiusz Kobus and Rafał Demkowicz-Dobrzański

We show an explicit [MATH]-qubit protocol involving one-axis-twisted spin squeezed states that allows for simultaneous phase and dephasing strength estimation with precision that asymptotically matches fundamental quantum metrological bounds. The relevance of the protocol goes beyond this particular mo…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022412] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an explicit qubit protocol using spin-squeezed states for simultaneous phase and dephasing estimation, achieving asymptotically optimal precision matching fundamental quantum metrological bounds.
motivation: The goal is to achieve optimal simultaneous estimation of phase and dephasing strength, which is a fundamental problem in quantum metrology and quantum information.
method: The authors propose a protocol using one-axis-twisted spin-squeezed states and analyze its performance using quantum Fisher information and multiparameter estimation theory.
result: The protocol asymptotically saturates the quantum Cramér-Rao bound for joint estimation, demonstrating optimal precision.
conclusion: The work provides a practical scheme for optimal multiparameter estimation, with implications for quantum sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Upper Bounds On The Purity Of Wigner Non-negative Quantum States That Verify The Wigner Entropy Conjecture
authors: Qipeng Qian And Christos N. Gagatsos
abstract:
Author(s): Qipeng Qian and Christos N. Gagatsos

We present analytical results toward the Wigner entropy conjecture, which posits that among all physical Wigner non-negative states, the Wigner entropy is minimized by pure Gaussian states for which it attains the value [MATH]. Working under a minimal set of constraints on the Wigner function, name…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022408] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides analytical upper bounds on the purity of Wigner non-negative states that satisfy the Wigner entropy conjecture, advancing the understanding of quantum entropy measures.
motivation: The Wigner entropy conjecture is a fundamental open problem in quantum information, linking Wigner entropy to Gaussian states. Proving or constraining it is important for characterizing non-classicality and information content of quantum states.
method: The authors work under minimal constraints on the Wigner function and derive analytical upper bounds on the purity of states that verify the conjecture, using techniques from quantum information theory and phase-space methods.
result: They obtain explicit upper bounds on purity for such states, providing partial progress toward proving the conjecture and offering insights into the structure of Wigner non-negative states.
conclusion: The results support the conjecture and provide a new tool for studying entropy measures in continuous-variable quantum information, with potential implications for quantum cryptography and thermodynamics.

title: Highly Robust Logical Qubit Encoding In An Ensemble Of V-symmetrical Qutrits
authors: Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Manuel Calixto, And Julio Guerrero
abstract:
Author(s): Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Manuel Calixto, and Julio Guerrero

We propose using even and odd Schrödinger cat states formed from coherent states of U(3) of an ensemble of qutrits with a symmetrical V configuration (a qubit-disguised qutrit) to encode a logical qubit. These carefully engineered logical qubit states are parameter-independent stationary states of t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033169] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes encoding a logical qubit in even and odd Schrödinger cat states of U(3) coherent states of an ensemble of V-symmetric qutrits, which are parameter-independent stationary states, offering a robust encoding scheme.
motivation: To achieve robust quantum information encoding in higher-dimensional systems, specifically using qutrits with a V configuration, which can be seen as qubit-disguised qutrits, to protect against certain errors.
method: The authors construct even and odd Schrödinger cat states from U(3) coherent states of an ensemble of qutrits with a symmetrical V configuration, and analyze their properties as logical qubit states.
result: The proposed logical qubit states are parameter-independent stationary states, indicating robustness against parameter variations, and the encoding scheme leverages the symmetry of the V configuration.
conclusion: The work provides a novel approach to logical qubit encoding using qutrit ensembles, potentially advancing quantum error correction and information processing.

title: Infinite Temperature At Zero Energy
authors: Matteo Ippoliti And David M. Long
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Ippoliti and David M. Long

Researchers construct local Hamiltonians whose eigenstates inherit infinite-temperature properties, producing ground states with extensive entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031030] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs local Hamiltonians whose ground states exhibit infinite-temperature properties, such as extensive entanglement, challenging conventional notions of ground states.
motivation: To explore the possibility of realizing infinite-temperature-like behavior in the ground states of local Hamiltonians, which could have implications for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.
method: The authors design specific local Hamiltonians and analyze their ground states, likely using analytical and numerical techniques to demonstrate the emergence of infinite-temperature properties.
result: They show that these Hamiltonians have ground states with extensive entanglement and other thermal-like properties, effectively realizing 'infinite temperature at zero energy'.
conclusion: The work provides a new class of Hamiltonians with exotic ground states, potentially relevant for quantum information and thermodynamics, though its direct applicability to the user's core interests is moderate.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To demonstrate a practical quantum advantage using a programmable ultracold-atom processor, which is a key platform in hybrid quantum systems.
method: The processor simulates the dynamics of a driven many-body system, likely using a Rydberg atom array or similar platform, and quantifies the computational advantage through benchmarking against classical simulations.
result: The experiment shows a clear quantum computational advantage, with the quantum processor outperforming classical methods in simulating the entangled dynamics.
conclusion: This work establishes ultracold-atom processors as viable platforms for achieving quantum advantage in many-body simulation, advancing the field of hybrid quantum systems.

title: Efficient Quantum Optimization Via Dynamical Simulation
authors: Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, And Nathan Wiebe
abstract:
Author(s): Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, and Nathan Wiebe

A gradient-free approach to quantum optimization based on coherent simulation of time evolution can outperform gradient-descent-based methods in query complexity and robustness to barren plateaus.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033026] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a gradient-free quantum optimization method based on coherent time evolution simulation, which achieves better query complexity and robustness to barren plateaus compared to gradient-descent methods.
motivation: Quantum optimization often suffers from barren plateaus and high query complexity in gradient-based methods. The authors aim to develop a more efficient and robust approach.
method: The method uses coherent simulation of time evolution to perform optimization without gradients, leveraging quantum dynamics to explore the parameter space.
result: The proposed method outperforms gradient-descent-based methods in query complexity and shows improved robustness to barren plateaus.
conclusion: Gradient-free quantum optimization via dynamical simulation is a promising alternative for quantum optimization, potentially advancing practical quantum computing.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a beam search decoder for quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes, achieving high accuracy and meeting real-time decoding latency requirements.
motivation: Real-time quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast, but existing decoders often trade off between these goals or demand massive classical resources.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoding algorithm tailored to QLDPC codes, which explores a limited set of candidate error patterns to balance accuracy and computational efficiency.
result: The decoder demonstrates high decoding accuracy while satisfying latency constraints for real-time operation, avoiding the need for extensive classical computation.
conclusion: The beam search decoder offers a practical solution for real-time decoding of QLDPC codes, advancing the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits at finite depths, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Understanding anticoncentration in noisy quantum circuits is crucial for quantum advantage and sampling tasks, but previous results were often architecture-specific or limited to asymptotic depths.
method: The authors analyze the spectral properties of the local noise and circuit architecture, deriving universal formulas for the anticoncentration of output probabilities as a function of depth and noise strength.
result: They identify distinct regimes (e.g., noise-dominated, circuit-dominated) and show that anticoncentration is universal across different architectures, with a crossover depth that depends on the noise rate.
conclusion: The findings provide a unified framework for predicting when noisy quantum circuits lose their computational advantage, with implications for benchmarking and error mitigation.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
